title: A Garden Beneath the Surface
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: When a group of students designed a rain garden for an imaginary school, their first drawing showed flowers surrounding a shallow depression.
sentences.ja: 架空の学校に雨水庭園を設計した生徒たちの最初の図には浅いくぼみを囲む花が描かれていた。

sentences.en: They expected visitors to judge the garden mainly by its appearance, especially during the months when the plants were in bloom.
sentences.ja: 訪問者は特に花の咲く時期に外観を中心に庭を評価すると予想した。

sentences.en: Their teacher asked them to draw a second diagram showing what might happen beneath the ground after a period of heavy rain.
sentences.ja: 教師は大雨後に地面の下で何が起こり得るか示す二枚目の図を描くよう求めた。

sentences.en: The question shifted their attention from visible decoration to processes that a casual observer might never notice.
sentences.ja: その問いは目に見える装飾から通りすがりの観察者には気づかれない過程へ注意を移した。

sentences.en: The group considered how different soil conditions could influence the movement of water through the proposed garden.
sentences.ja: 生徒は土壌条件の違いが計画された庭の水の移動にどう影響するか考えた。

sentences.en: A surface that looked attractive in dry weather might behave quite differently when exposed to a large quantity of water.
sentences.ja: 乾燥時に魅力的な地表も大量の水にさらされると全く異なる振る舞いをするかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students realized that selecting plants without considering their relationship to surrounding conditions would leave a substantial part of the design unexplained.
sentences.ja: 周囲条件との関係を考えず植物を選ぶと設計のかなりの部分が説明されないと気づいた。

sentences.en: They also recognized that their classroom drawings could not establish the actual drainage capacity of a site without further investigation.
sentences.ja: 教室の図だけでは追加調査なしに敷地の実際の排水能力を確定できないとも認識した。

sentences.en: Rather than promising that the proposed garden would prevent flooding, the students identified questions that a more detailed site assessment would need to address.
sentences.ja: 庭が洪水を防ぐと約束するのでなく、より詳細な敷地評価で扱うべき問いを特定した。

sentences.en: They included the direction of runoff, existing underground structures, and the maintenance requirements of different planting arrangements.
sentences.ja: 流出水の方向、既存地下構造物、異なる植栽配置の管理要件を含めた。

sentences.en: The project therefore became an exercise in identifying relationships rather than selecting a collection of individually attractive objects.
sentences.ja: 活動は個別に魅力的な物を集めるのでなく関係を特定する練習になった。

sentences.en: The students prepared labels explaining both the intended function of the garden and the limitations of their preliminary design.
sentences.ja: 庭の意図した機能と予備設計の限界を説明するラベルを作った。

sentences.en: During a fictional exhibition, a visitor asked why the group had devoted so much space to drawings of invisible processes.
sentences.ja: 架空の展示で来場者はなぜ見えない過程の図に多くの場所を使ったか尋ねた。

sentences.en: One student replied that a beautiful surface could conceal weaknesses in the system responsible for supporting it.
sentences.ja: 美しい表面がそれを支える仕組みの弱点を隠す可能性があると答えた。

sentences.en: Another explained that the garden's ecological performance could not reasonably be inferred from a photograph taken on a single sunny day.
sentences.ja: 晴天一日の写真から生態学的性能を合理的に推論できないと別の生徒が説明した。

sentences.en: The diagrams helped visitors understand why evaluating the design would require observations under a variety of conditions over time.
sentences.ja: 図は設計評価に時間をかけ多様な条件で観察が必要な理由を理解する助けになった。

sentences.en: This imagined project illustrates that environmental design involves more than producing an attractive final image of a proposed landscape.
sentences.ja: この仮想活動は環境設計に景観の魅力的な完成図以上のことが必要だと示す。

sentences.en: The arrangement of visible elements may be important, but the relationships between those elements and less obvious processes also deserve careful examination.
sentences.ja: 目に見える要素の配置は重要でも、要素と見えにくい過程の関係も慎重な検討に値する。

sentences.en: A responsible proposal should distinguish the benefits it aims to achieve from the evidence needed to demonstrate that those benefits have actually been achieved.
sentences.ja: 責任ある提案は目指す利益と実際に達成したことを示すための根拠を区別すべきだ。

sentences.en: In this case, the most useful drawing was not necessarily the one that looked most complete, but the one that revealed which questions remained unanswered.
sentences.ja: この場合最も有用な図は必ずしも最も完成して見えるものではなく未解決の問いを明らかにするものだった。

questions.prompt: What did the first drawing emphasize?
options: Visible plants and the garden's appearance.
To examine processes hidden beneath the surface.
questions.explanation_ja: 見えない過程への注意。

options: Drawings alone cannot determine actual drainage capacity.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の能力は図だけで確定しない。

questions.prompt: What did the group identify instead of promising flood prevention?
How did the nature of the project change?
options: It became a competition for the prettiest flowers.
It focused on relationships between elements.

questions.prompt: Why did the group include diagrams of invisible processes?
options: Visitors could not see any flowers.
Surface appearance can hide functional weaknesses.
questions.explanation_ja: 外観では機能が分からない。

questions.prompt: Why were observations over time needed?
options: A single photograph cannot establish ecological performance.
All visitors use the same route.

questions.prompt: Which idea best summarizes the passage?
options: A beautiful garden always prevents flooding.
Environmental design should explain hidden relationships and distinguish aims from demonstrated results.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的と実証を区別する。

grammar.focus: that a casual observer might never notice
from the evidence needed to demonstrate

paraphrases.source: The question shifted their attention from visible decoration to processes that a casual observer might never notice.
paraphrases.rewrite: The question drew attention to processes not easily visible to visitors.

paraphrases.source: The students realized that selecting plants without considering their relationship to surrounding conditions would leave a substantial part of the design unexplained.
paraphrases.rewrite: Plant selection alone would leave important environmental relationships unexplained.

paraphrases.source: Rather than promising that the proposed garden would prevent flooding, the students identified questions that a more detailed site assessment would need to address.
paraphrases.rewrite: They identified questions for further assessment instead of guaranteeing flood prevention.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 効果を保証せず調査項目を示す。

paraphrases.source: A responsible proposal should distinguish the benefits it aims to achieve from the evidence needed to demonstrate that those benefits have actually been achieved.
paraphrases.rewrite: A good proposal separates its goals from the evidence that would establish their achievement.

discourse.role_ja: 外観評価の時期を限定。
可視要素と見えない過程の対比。
